Sure, that was part of it. Rome also had a system where various rich guys owned much of the government, and couldn't agree among themselves about priorities. Rome had infrastructure problems. Rome had corruption problems. Rome tried to govern an area which was too big to be managed using the communication- and supply-chains available in their time. There was a log going on, too many points-of-failure, and too many of them went south all at once. It was bound to happen sooner or later. Surprising that the Roman Empire lasted as long as it did.

The thing is there have been proposed many causes for the fall of Rome. this list alone lists 210 reasons (some humorous, some very likely wrong). Another thing to remember is that this article only refers to the Western Roman Empire. The Eastern part survived for another 1000 years, many of these years it was a dominant power.

Lastly remember that making a clear comparison between today and something that happened 1700 years ago is almost impossible. The world was a vastly different place back then. Any comparison requires a lot of good will and belief on the one making the comparison.
